messages.author: e56677c713174601
messages.subject: How to add Nest Production rate and Nest Decay time as a multipliers fir line transects
parts:
Hi,
I'm trying to analyze data from a chimpanzee nest counting survey. In order to fo this as much accurate as possible I want to introduce the Nest Production rate, the Nest Decay time and the Nest Building proportion. I already know that they can be introduced as a multipliers, but I do not find the way to do it. Can you help me, please?
Thansk in advance,
Guillem

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] How to add Nest Production rate and Nest Decay time as a multipliers fir line transects
parts:
Guillem

Thanks for your question.  I can see from the screenshot you have provided, you have used the Multipliers tab in the Model Definition window to specify fields in your data that contain the multipliers.  What does not seem correct to me is that you have specified the same field name for the multiplier, its standard error and its degrees of freedom.

Because there is uncertainty in both the disappearance and production rate, values of that uncertainty should be available.  Those measures of uncertainty would be recorded in your data so that the uncertainty in the multipliers can be propagated into the uncertainty in the chimpanzee abundance estimate.

After correctly specifying the fields for standard error of the multipliers and perhaps the degrees of freedom (optionally), you have otherwise set up your multipliers properly.  That should be all the information needed by Distance to produce chimpanzee estimates.  Distance will detect there is information regarding multipliers in your project and put that information to use.

We have a lecture and exercise online regarding the use of multipliers.  Have a look at the lecture "Multipliers" and exercise "Exercise using multipliers" in Chapter 6 of our online materials:
https://workshops.distancesampling.org/online-course/syllabus/Chapter6/

Let me know if you have other questions.

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] How to add Nest Production rate and Nest Decay time as a multipliers fir line transects
parts:
Thanks for the clarification Guillem.

If you do not have values for the SE and DF, then do not put anything into those slots in the multiplier tab.  Simply leave those entries in the multipliers table empty.  Distance will use the information provided and not generate an error if SE and/or DF is missing.  Recognise that without SE for multipliers, the uncertainty in chimp abundance will be an underestimate.  You should note that in the report of your findings you produce.

I only have the Nest Decay time and its SE, the Nest Production rate and the Nest builders proportion. As far as I understood the SE and the DF are optional, but I do not know how to ignore in them and use only the information I have in the Multipliers. Can you tell me how to do that, please?
Thank you in advance,
Guillem
